messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got back from the market—saw the same old faces, same jokes at the checkpoints. Feels quiet, too quiet, like the air’s holding its breath. But the bonds sold out, the stats came out on time, and even the retired colonel said it’s the calmest he’s seen in years. Whatever’s coming, they’re not panicking."
Sender 2: "The air feels different—quiet, but charged. People are watching, talking in circles, but no one’s stepping forward yet. Still, the signs are piling up, and something’s shifting beneath the surface."
Sender 3: "The kids came home quiet today—no chatter about protests or rumors, just regular homework and stories from class. Feels like the air’s been sucked out of the streets, and the silence is louder than anything. Just keep it close, and watch the quiet."
Sender 4: "Just heard the new hospital wing opened last week—my friend in radiology said it was packed, but in a good way. Seems like things are moving on schedule, even the big conference abroad is confirmed. Honestly, everything's quiet, in a way that feels… normal."
Sender 5: "Just had a quiet chat with someone from the old circle—same as us, they’re feeling the same quiet unease. Feels like we’re all holding our breath, waiting to see if the ground shifts or just stays still."
Sender 6: "The weather’s been strange this season—too dry, too still. I’ve been thinking about the school garden project; maybe we should finish planting early, just in case."
Sender 7: "The air feels different—people are talking more, moving cautiously, like they’re testing the ground. Whatever’s brewing, it’s not just nerves; the system’s moving slower, and even the usual quiet is uneasy."
Sender 8: "The quiet is holding — weddings are happening, payments are late but coming, and the palace feels too calm for anything brewing. Still, the real test will be how long this stillness lasts."
Sender 9: "Just got word from the clinic — they’ve been quietly restocking meds, same as last month. Feels like everyone’s holding their breath, but the quiet’s not anxious, just… settled. Maybe it’s nothing, but the air’s different — like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying where it’s going."
Sender 10: "The air feels different lately—people are talking more, even cautiously. Just had a quiet coffee with someone who mentioned the same odd clicking in their phone; small things, but they’re not just in my head. Keep it light, stay sharp."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
